title: Audit-append **concurrency contention.** `SqlAuditSink` takes no application-level lock: two genuinely concurrent state-changing requests both read the same chain tip (`TipHashAsync`) and race the `audit.AuditEvents` `PreviousHash` UNIQUE index — the loser gets SQL error 2601 (duplicate key) and the whole operation **500s** (fail-closed, but a hard error rather than a retry). Accepted at design time (ADR-0009/0026 + the `SqlAuditSink.cs` `ponytail:` note — "negligible at ≤20-user on-prem scale; if it ever bites, serialize via `sp_getapplock` or retry"). **Reproduced 2026-07-13** by the P15b live VR: the SPA's login-time `Membership.ProfileSynced` append raced an immediate seed burst, so one `Research.MissionProposed` lost the race and 500'd (audit seq 12/13 both chained off tip `1f738021`). Fix (the pre-named upgrade path): a **bounded retry** on 2601/2627 inside `AppendAsync` — re-read tip, recompute hash, re-insert — which preserves chain linearity + the fail-closed guarantee; or `sp_getapplock` serialization. **2026-07-13 — operator chose to fix now**, then (after adversarial review) to fix it **robustly** rather than cheaply. Arc: a first pass added a bounded optimistic-retry in `SqlAuditSink`; CI then showed the 8-way stress case **deadlocks (SQL 1205)**, whose victim's transaction is rolled back → in-place retry cannot recover. A devil's-advocate review further found a **sink-level app lock is lock-order-unsafe** (handlers like `IssueDecision`/`VerifyAction` emit-then-write-more, inverting `{lock, module-rows}` order). **✅ RESOLVED 2026-07-13 via ADR-0028 (serialize at tx-open):** `AmbientTransaction.EnsureStartedAsync` takes a **transaction-scoped exclusive `sp_getapplock`** ('acmp-audit-chain') immediately after `BeginTransaction` — before any module write — so every audited write-command acquires the chain lock first (one consistent order → no cross-handler deadlock) and appends serialize (no fork, no 1205). Held to commit ⇒ next command reads a committed tip; `THROW` on lock-timeout ⇒ fail-closed; SQL-Server-only (degrades to no-op elsewhere). The **denial/autocommit path** (no ambient tx) keeps the bounded retry as its backstop (broadened to catch the `PreviousHash` **or** `Hash` index race; deadlock-free — no crosswise module locks). Tests: `Concurrent_commands_all_commit_without_forking_the_audit_chain` (8 write-commands serialize) + `Concurrent_denials_all_record_their_audit_via_the_retry_without_forking_the_chain` (8 denials converge via retry) + the same-tx atomicity suite, all green (CI-proven for the write-command deadlock case). No schema/migration.

title: **Flaky frontend test — `src/Acmp.Web/src/features/decisions/DecisionPage.test.tsx:174`.** Intermittently reads `/decisions/DECN-2026-008` where `/decisions/DECN-2026-015` is expected; unrelated red on the D-18 PR #111 CI run 2026-07-13, green on the immediate re-run. **⚠ The original diagnosis recorded here was wrong** and is corrected in place (P17a, 2026-07-17): it blamed "non-deterministic decision selection (order-/hash-dependent pick over the mocked decisions list)" — **there is no decisions list and no selection in that test.** `useDecision` is mocked to one fixed object (`:54-56`) and the supersede mutation is a fixed `mockResolvedValue({ key: 'DECN-2026-015' })` (`:78`); both are deterministic. **Real mechanism:** `DECN-2026-008` is simply `setup()`'s initial route (`:62`), and `DECN-2026-015` is reachable only *after* `SupersedeDialog.onConfirm` awaits `mutateAsync` and then calls `navigate()` (`SupersedeDialog.tsx:70-81`). The assertion read `expect(await screen.findByTestId('loc')).toHaveTextContent(...)` — but `loc` (`LocationDisplay`) is **always mounted**, so `findByTestId` resolved on its first poll without waiting for anything, and `toHaveTextContent` then evaluated **exactly once** against a pathname the post-await `navigate()` may not yet have flushed. Hence the initial route, and hence why a re-run passes. **Scope note:** the sibling sync assertions at `:168`/`:188`/`:209`/`:217-220` are **not** affected — `mutateAsync` is *invoked* synchronously inside `onConfirm`, so an awaited `user.click` guarantees the call happened; only code after the handler's own `await` races. They were deliberately left untouched.
activation_trigger: **✅ Done 2026-07-17 (P17a)** — retry the *assertion* rather than the element: `await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByTestId('loc')).toHaveTextContent('/decisions/DECN-2026-015'))`. `:235` left as-is (sync `getByTestId` asserting the path *stays* on the error path — correct there, and preceded by a real `findByText` await).

title: **Inline `style={{}}` usage in the SPA — style hygiene, NOT a security control.** ~110 inline-style sites across ~25 components (18 static, 7 dynamic + `SortableList.tsx`'s @dnd-kit drag transform). P16-B3 planned to refactor them all (static → CSS classes, dynamic → a `useCssVars` CSSOM hook, plus a @dnd-kit CSSOM shim) in order to drop `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`. **Verified 2026-07-16 that the refactor is unnecessary for that goal:** CSP governs `<style>` elements and `style=""` attributes, not the CSSOM, and react-dom applies the `style` prop via CSSOM writes (`style.setProperty(...)` / `style[name] = v` — confirmed in the react-dom source), never serialising a style attribute. With no SSR (client-rendered Vite SPA), no inline style in `index.html`, DOMPurify's allowlist excluding `style` attrs + `<style>` tags, and no CSS-in-JS dependency, `style-src 'self'` ships **with the code as-is** (browser-verified: CSSOM writes apply, `setAttribute('style')` and injected `<style>` are blocked). C-WEB-02 is therefore **Met without this work**.
activation_trigger: A frontend consistency/design-system pass elects to take it on. **Do not activate for CSP reasons** — that rationale is disproven.

title: ADR-0038 DEPLOY PLUMBING (§5) — DONE 2026-08-12 (PR #237, main 122f41d). What shipped, and how it differs from the plan this row was raised with: THE CLIENT IS DEFINED IN reconcile.sh, NOT IN realm-export.json (DEF-049). Keycloak imports the bundled export only on FIRST run, so a client declared there reaches a fresh stack and never appears on prod or UAT — the DEF-023 / CHANGE-004 seam a third time. The client SECRET settled it: a secret can only be made to match gen-secrets' file by being SET from that file, so the client cannot be expressed in the export at all. reconcile.sh now creates-or-updates the client, re-asserts confidential + service-account-only on every run, sets the secret FROM the mounted file, and RECONCILES THE GRANT AS AN EXACT SET — revoking anything outside it, so a widened grant cannot survive a deploy — then reads the result back rather than trusting exit codes. THE GRANT IS `manage-users` AND NOTHING ELSE (OQ-070), and it now has a gate: check-realm-export.mjs asserts the EXACT set with realm-admin named forbidden, and BOTH failure branches were proven by forcing them (adding view-realm; granting realm-admin). The grant lives in deploy/keycloak/admin-client.env so the gate and the reconciler read the SAME value — a check reading a different file passes while the deployment drifts — and it needed a .gitignore exception, because `*.env` would have silently excluded the one file both of them depend on (the gate passed locally only because the file existed on disk). ENABLING IS ONE VARIABLE, which removes the boot-stopping sequencing hazard this row was raised warning about: the secret is ALWAYS written, unlike the Webex block, because a compose secrets: entry whose file is missing fails the whole stack, and because ValidateOnStart means a flag arriving before its secret STOPS api and worker rather than degrading. 09-put-env.sh now refuses that exact combination at the last point before it reaches a machine; gen-secrets GENERATES a value when unset rather than failing, so an operator .env predating the variable still boots — with no literal fallback, because a default credential in a script is a credential. The worker got identical config: it composes the same Membership module, so a flag without a secret would fail ITS validator too. VERIFIED SAFE FOR THE LIVE BOX BEFORE MERGING: 08-bootstrap-box.sh:164 runs gen-secrets BEFORE compose up at :207, so the new secret file always exists on a real deploy. ⚠ WHAT IS NOT YET EVIDENCED, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: that the reconciler actually CREATED the client anywhere. CI's e2e boots the full stack against a real Keycloak and passed, but DEF-051 records that nothing depends on keycloak-config — so a failed reconcile leaves the stack healthy, and A GREEN E2E IS NOT EVIDENCE THE CLIENT EXISTS. Closing that assertion is DEF-051's job; the AC-090 behavioural leg additionally needs a deploy with KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ENABLED=true.

title: GUEST ACCESS WINDOWS FOLLOW THE MEETING - DONE 2026-08-12 (PR #244, main 5afe40f), and the row's own premise turned out to be FALSE. As raised this row said 'rescheduling a meeting does not move a guest's already-written window'. ACMP HAS NO RESCHEDULE: Meeting.ScheduledStart/End are private-set and assigned only in the Schedule factory, there is no PUT/PATCH on /api/meetings, and no feature mutates them - three independent checks. A meeting is scheduled once, then started, held or cancelled. So nothing was built for reschedule; IGuestWindowWriter takes an arbitrary instant precisely so a future reschedule can call it with the new end plus GuestAccess.Grace. WHAT DID SHIP is what DEC-041 added when it widened the scope, and those are the EXPOSURE cases rather than the inconvenience one: cancelling a meeting CLOSES its guest presenters' windows (an outsider must not keep live read access to material for a meeting that will not happen); removing the agenda item CLOSES it (the slot the access was granted for is gone); reassigning the slot CLOSES the replaced guest's window, while re-assigning the SAME person is a no-op. DESIGN NOTE WORTH KEEPING: IGuestWindowWriter is a SEPARATE port from IGuestProvisioner for availability, not tidiness - the provisioner is registered only when the Keycloak admin client is configured, so folding this in would have made CANCELLING A MEETING FAIL wherever in-app user management is off, which is every environment today. This port creates nothing (one nullable column) so it is registered unconditionally, like IPrincipalRevalidator. TWO SAFETY PROPERTIES, both proven by tests rather than argued: a guest holding a SECOND slot keeps their access (the rule is 'close it only if they no longer present any slot on a live meeting', checked against the store after the change, not reasoned about); and an ORDINARY member never acquires an expiry, because the port only touches rows that already hold a window - a member handed one by accident would be locked out of the whole product and DEF-029 means the row could never be deleted to recover.
activation_trigger: Reschedule: if a reschedule feature is ever built, it must call IGuestWindowWriter with the new ScheduledEnd + GuestAccess.Grace. Nothing else outstanding.

title: Stream.IsWildcard SHIPS WITH NO PRODUCTION READER, DELIBERATELY - and that is DW-026's exact signature, so it is registered here rather than left to be re-discovered as a fifth instance. WHAT LANDED (ADR-0042 step 1, PR 'feat/def-057-step1-seed-streams'): a bool column on membership.streams, a filtered unique index enforcing at most one wildcard row, and a seed of the committee's five delivery streams plus the wildcard. WHAT DOES NOT EXIST YET: any code that READS the column. Grep IsWildcard after this PR and you get the entity property, the EF configuration, the migration and the integration tests - and no production consumer. That is precisely how Topic.Reopen, Stream.Create, StreamScopeRequirement and Topic.SetScope each presented, so a reviewer applying DW-026's own lesson SHOULD flag this. This row is the answer to that flag. WHY IT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT, and the reasoning is ADR-0042's ordering, which the ADR calls load-bearing and non-negotiable: the reader is the authorization path, and wiring the authorization path before every member has been assigned a stream locks the entire committee out (all 26 production members were seeded straight into Keycloak, so the invite-time stream field does not cover them - ADR-0042 consequence (1), the one marked CERTAIN). The column must therefore EXIST, and be seeded, several PRs before anything consults it. Landing them together is the failure mode the ADR explicitly warns about: 'anyone treating it as one change will land the seed without the parts that make it safe'. THE NAMED FUTURE READER, so this is not an open-ended promise: UserStreamProvider (Membership.Infrastructure/Authorization/MembershipAbacProviders.cs), consumed by StreamScopeHandler, at ADR-0042 STEP 7. ⚠ THE READER CANNOT BE ADDED WITHOUT A PORT CHANGE, which is the real reason it is not a one-line follow-up: IUserStreamProvider.GetAssignedStreamsAsync returns IReadOnlyCollection<string> - a bare list of stream CODES. Wildcard-ness cannot travel through that return type without matching on the wildcard's code, which is EXACTLY what ADR-0042 clause (3) forbids (a magic string in an authorization control breaks silently on rename or re-code, or hands universal access to a future stream that collides with it). So step 7 must widen the port to carry the assigned codes AND a HasWildcard flag - symmetric with the AffectsAllStreams primitive bool that ADR-0042 clause (6) already mandates on IStreamScopedResource for the same cross-module reason (ADR-0001: the contract lives in Acmp.Shared.Contracts, the enum in Topics.Domain; ADR-0021 is the pattern). ⚠ UNTIL STEP 7 LANDS, ASSIGNING THE WILDCARD STREAM TO A MEMBER GRANTS NOTHING AND REFUSES NOTHING - it is inert data. It is not a latent bypass: no code path consults it, so it cannot widen access. The genuine risk in the interval is the opposite one - an administrator assigning 'All streams' through the (still to be built) UI and reasonably believing it took effect. That is why the assignment UI is step 3 and the wiring is step 7, with the backfill at step 5 in between. INVARIANT AT STAKE: same as DW-026 - a control that is never evaluated is indistinguishable from an implemented one. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-15 (DEC-048 d1): THE TRIGGER FIRED AND THE PREMISE IS NO LONGER TRUE. The column now has THREE production readers - UserStreamProvider reads it and returns IsUnrestricted from ONE query (a flag from a column, never a code match, exactly as ADR-0042 clause (3) required), StreamScopeRequirement consumes that verdict, and the DEC-046 reconciliation grants that stream to every member row it creates. The port widening this row predicted as the blocker is what step 7 actually did. ⚠ What is NOT claimed by closing this: the wildcard path has not yet run in PRODUCTION - that is DEF-065's deploy step and is tracked there, not here.
activation_trigger: ADR-0042 step 7 (wiring StreamScopeRequirement into the stream-bounded write policies). Close this row when UserStreamProvider reports wildcard-ness through the widened port and a test proves a wildcard-holding member is granted where an unassigned one is refused. ⚠ If ADR-0042 is ever abandoned before step 7, this column and its seed must be REMOVED rather than left - an unread column with no owning plan is the debt DW-026 describes.

title: THE /session PRESENTER PREVIEW IS DECIDED BUT NOT BUILT — OQ-074 resolved to 'a chosen presenter's slot' (DEC-048 d4) and answering the question shipped no code. Registered so the decision does not read as delivery. WHAT IS NEEDED, and it is three things rather than one: (1) A TARGETING PARAMETER on the /session read path — an explicit target (meeting + topic, or member) that identifies WHOSE slot is rendered, where today the endpoint answers for the caller and nothing else. (2) AUTHORIZATION ON THAT PARAMETER, which is the part with teeth: only Chairman and Secretary may pass it, and a GUEST passing it must be refused as firmly as a Secretary is served. This is precisely the 'second code path to keep correct' DEC-037 flagged when it opened the route, and it is a second authorization path over content scoped to SOMEBODY ELSE — the shape that produced DEF-052 (fourteen content groups with no read-side role gate) and DEF-056 (a refusal nobody audits). Treat the refusal as the feature and prove it by forcing it. (3) AN ENTRY-POINT AFFORDANCE, which is NOT a nav item. ⚠ navModel.ts's ACCESS map grants `session` to GUEST ONLY, and OQ-074 established before the decision that reading (b) 'would not be a session nav item at all' — the preview starts from a chosen presenter, so the natural entry is from the meeting or agenda surface where that presenter is already listed. DEF-053 deliberately did not touch the ACCESS map to avoid pre-empting this decision, and that restraint still holds: the map stays guest-only. WHY THIS IS DEFERRED RATHER THAN BUILT NOW: nobody has yet asked to preview a specific presenter, the guest-facing /session page works, and the cost is a new authorization surface — which is exactly the kind of thing this project builds when it is needed and not before (the same reasoning that kept the reconciliation UI unbuilt). INVARIANT AT STAKE: INV-014 for the entry point (compose from the design system, and flag it as a no-reference composition since no .dc.html covers a presenter-preview affordance), and permission-role-matrix E.3 for the authorization — a guest is bounded by a TIME WINDOW, so a targeting parameter must never become the way a guest reads somebody else's slot.
activation_trigger: When the Secretary or Chairman actually needs to preview a presenter's view — in practice, before the first meeting that has guest presenters and a rehearsal step. ⚠ It is NOT triggered by the DEF-065 deploy: /session already works for guests, and this adds an affordance for the two roles that never presents anything to a guest.

title: EVIDENCE THE 162 REQUIREMENTS THAT HAVE NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — the real remediation behind DEF-012, separated from it because it is a programme rather than a defect fix. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DEFINES THE WORK, taken 2026-08-16: this package holds 222 requirements; EXACTLY 60 have at least one active acceptance criterion and EXACTLY those 60 are Implemented; EXACTLY 162 have NO acceptance criterion and EXACTLY those 162 are Approved. The correlation is perfect, and it is mechanical rather than coincidental: a requirement advances to Implemented ONLY through the auto-advance trigger, which fires when every non-retired AC of that requirement has a latest verdict of Met, so a requirement with no ACs can never advance no matter how thoroughly it shipped. CONSEQUENCE: requirement status in this package is a proxy for 'did anyone write an acceptance criterion', not for 'was this built'. Everything downstream inherits that — v_backlog lists all 155 wbs_items as open (DEF-012), and any reader treating requirement status as a completion signal is reading a coverage statistic instead. INVARIANT AT STAKE, stated here because the column is a foreign key and no invariant row covers it: the package is the record, and a status that reflects whether anyone WROTE an acceptance criterion rather than whether the thing was BUILT makes every downstream view a coverage statistic wearing the costume of a completion signal. WHAT THE WORK IS: for each of the 162, either write an acceptance criterion and audit it with evidence, or record explicitly that the requirement is not separately verifiable and why. ⚠ IT MUST NOT BE DONE BY BULK-ADVANCING REQUIREMENT STATUS — that is the manufactured-status failure DEF-010 records, and DEF-012's own row already refuses the equivalent shortcut for work items. ⚠ AND IT MUST NOT BE DONE BY THE MECHANICAL SHORTCUT THAT LOOKS SOUND: 'close a work item when every requirement it names is Implemented' was tried and is UNSOUND — it closes WBS-20.4, the email adapter, on the strength of the Implemented FR-130, while 'no email in v1, in-app centre only' is a hard constraint of this project (DEC-055). SIZING, so nobody starts it casually: 162 requirements, each needing an AC written, bound to a slice, and audited with evidence against a commit.
